title: WPSB/294/2014 of Dr Arvind Kumar Singh AND ANOTHER Vs Uttarakhand Technical University AND OTHERS

paras.text:
Reserved Judgment
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Review Application MCC no. 182 of 2016
Review Application MCC no. 201 of 2016
in
Writ Petition no. 193 (S/B) of 2014
Faculty Association THDC & others ....... Petitioners
 versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ....... Respondents
with

Review Application MCC no. 199 of 2016
Review Application MCC no. 213 of 2016
in
Writ Petition no. 294 (S/B) of 2014
Dr. Arvind Kumar Singh & another .......... Petitioners
 versus
Uttarakhand Technical University&others .......... Respondents

Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Lalit Samant and Mr.
Shailendra Nauriyal, Advocates for respondent Uttarakhand Technical University
/ review applicant(s).
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate for THDC Institute of Hydro Power Engineering
and Technology (respondent no. 5) / Review applicant(s).
Coram : Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.

Per: U.C. Dhyani, J.
 Aforementioned review applications have been
filed separately on behalf of applicants, namely, THDC
Institute of Hydropower Engineering & Technology and
Uttarakhand Technical University with the following
prayer, among others:
"to allow the present review applications and
quash the order / judgment dated 01.12.2015,
passed by this Court in Writ Petition no. 193 of

2
2014 (S/B), Faculty Association and others vs
State of Uttarakhand and others as well as in Writ
Petition no. 294 of 2014 (S/B), Dr. Arvind Kumar
Singh and another vs Uttarakhand Technical
University and others, in toto."
2) On 01.12.2015, this Court had decided Writ
petition no. 193 of 2014 (S/B) and Writ Petition no. 294 of
2014 (S/B). It was also directed, while deciding the
aforesaid writ petitions, that all the interim orders to the
contrary, if any, stand vacated.
3) Now review applications have been filed on
behalf of the applicants, namely THDC Institute of
Hydropower Engineering & Technology and Uttarakhand
Technical University, in both the aforesaid writ petitions,
on the following grounds:
i) The Court has failed to consider the fact that vide
order dated 03.03.2015, it had directed to constitute
the Committee to evaluate the educational
qualification of the petitioners and it was observed
that if the petitioners do not fulfill the required
educational qualifications than it would be in the
fitness of things to consider their services as purely
temporary in nature. The Court has also failed to
consider the fact that the Committee duly constituted
as per directions given by the Court vide order dated
03.03.2015 found that some of the petitioners are not
eligible and not fit for the alleged posts.
ii) The Court has failed to consider the fact that there is
no substantive post in the Institute and, therefore, no
regularization can be done, as it is a settled principle

3
of law that no regularization can be made unless and
until there exists a substantive post.
iii) The Court has failed to consider the fact that
University as per the MOU executed between THDC
and the University clearly states that University shall
recruit and appoint all teaching and non-teaching staff
required for running the Institute as per AICTE
norms. It was also mentioned that University shall
pay salaries and all associated expenses of staff as per
AICTE/UGC norms and pay scales.
iv) It was not presented before the Court that on
09.02.2011, a meeting was held under the
Chairmanship of Principal Secretary, Technical
Education Department, Uttarakhand in relation to
establishment of THDC-IHET as constituent college
of UTU. In the meeting, it was decided with
consensus that THDC-IHET Institute shall run as a
self finance Institute. It was also decided that before
making THDC-IHET a constituent college of UTU,
an approval / No objection from the Government will
be taken and before signing MOU between University
and THDC Ltd., the MOU shall be approved from the
Government of Uttarakhand. It is pertinent to
mention here that MOU signed between the
University and THDC India Ltd. was not approved
from the Govt. of Uttarakhand and was also not
legally vetted by the legal department of Uttarakhand
Government. This is a reason why some points of
MOU are not in accord with Uttarakhand Technical
University Act, 2005. Moreover, the MOU executed
between University and THDC India Ltd. has not
been approved by the Executive Council of the

4
University. Therefore, the MOU has no legal sanctity
and it cannot override the provisions of the University
Act, 2005.
v) It was also not presented before the Court that in
expert / selection committee meeting dated
07.06.2012, the committee was not even empowered
to regularize or to make any recommendation for such
regularization as the post was not available and,
therefore, no regularization can be made in year
2011-12. The committee had only found already
working faculty as suitable and recommended for
their continuation.
vi) The Court has failed to consider the fact that the
selection of faculty recruited in the year 2011-12 and
further in the year 2012-13 was not as per the norms
of UGC/AICTE/State Government. The finding of
the committee constituted in compliance of this
Court's order dated 03.03.2015 is self-explanatory to
the fact that the selection was not done as per the
UGC/AICTE norms, because the committee had
found few faculty not qualified for the posts against
which they were providing their services.
vii) The Court has failed to consider the fact that the
regularization of the faculty is directly against the
proposition of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court
in State of Karnataka vs Umadevi, (2006) 4 SCC 1.
viii) The Court has failed to consider the fact the
University has no power to create the post as the post
can only be created by the State Government as per
the provision of Section 6(j) of the Uttarakhand
Technical University Act, 2005.

5
ix) The Court has failed to consider that most of the
petitioners are not eligible as per report dated
06.06.2015 of the committee headed by Chief
Secretary. Furthermore, the petitioners who are not
eligible cannot be permitted to work as per the
guidelines of the UGC / AICTE.
x) The court has failed to consider the fact that
petitioners cannot be regularized unless the posts are
created and regularization of the petitioners cannot be
done against the norms and guidelines of the UGC /
AICTE, as standard of the education is required to be
maintained and that the University and the Institute
are bound to follow the guidelines laid down by UGC
/ AICTE in this regard.
xi) The Court has failed to consider the fact that
Memorandum of Understanding executed between
THDC India Limited and Uttarakhand Technical
University says that the Institute shall be run by the
Uttarakhand Technical University. The State
Government has pervasive control over the
Uttarakhand Technical University, and the THDC
Institute of Hydropower Engineering and
Technology, Bhagirathpuram, Tehri, Uttarakhand was
established after obtaining No Objection Certificate
given to the University by the State Government. The
State Government is the only competent authority to
frame the First Regulation dealing with the subject
mentioned above and the posts can be created only
after such Regulation is made by the State
Government.
xii) The Court has failed to consider the fact that teachers
in the University in different posts were appointed for

6
a period of one year with the stipulation that they
shall be considered in second phase of interview
against permanent positions and those who have
served one year probation may be relaxed. The self
appraisal performance index will be sole criteria for
final interview. The reading of the provision would
suggest that there is no assurance that they shall be
regularized on the posts they are working.
xiii) The Court failed to consider that the University in the
year 2012 regularized the services of certain teaching
staff putting the person on one year probation from
the date of joining without any post duly sanctioned
by the State Government. Since the State Government
has not sanctioned the post in three constituent
colleges situated in the State of Uttarakhand,
including THDC Institute of Hydropower
Engineering and Technology, Bhagirathpuram, Tehri
and on coming to know that the appointments in these
colleges are being made without any sanctioned post,
therefore, the Government Order dated 23.07.2012
was issued to stop the recruitment process. In
continuation thereof a Government Order dated
16.08.2012 was issued by which it was provided that
in all three constituent colleges the appointment will
be made on contract basis till the sanction of the post
and consequently the University vide its corrigendum
letter dated 14.08.2012 has withdrawn the order of
regularization. Further it is relevant to mention that
the petitioner accepted the said condition /
corrigendum and further their services were renewed,
after the submission of their PBAS forms as per the
direction of this Court in the present case, for next

7
academic session and, therefore, the petitioners have
no right to challenge the same as they are barred by
their conduct/estoppel. The services of the petitioners
were renewed and they accepted, as the said
conditions were mentioned in the renewal letter
indicating the fact that their services shall be extended
on the basis of their PBAS form.
xiv) The Court has failed to consider that so far as
question of regularization is concerned, it is an
admitted fact that the initial appointment of all the
petitioners were on temporary / contractual / adhoc
basis for a fixed period of one year. The
advertisement also suggests that the post has been
advertised for one year only. There is also no dispute
that the appointment was made for a period of one
year only. Now the question which arises for
consideration is -as to whether the person appointed
for a period of one year can claim regularization on
the said post, as for regularization of service there
must be a rule for regularization. There must be a
sanctioned post on which the regularization can be
made and the other most essential requirement is that
the person claiming regularization must be appointed
by a due process of law against a substantive vacancy,
but in the present case, none of the requirements are
fulfilled, therefore, no regularization of services can
be made.
xv) The Court has failed to consider the fact that mere
continuance of service on temporary, Adhoc and
contractual basis does not confer any right to be
considered for absorption in service.

8
xvi) The Court has failed to consider that petitioners from
the date of filing of the petition has made several
applications without making amendment in the
pleading, therefore, all the applications may be
treated as interlocutory applications and no reference
can be made on these applications at the time of final
disposal and the issue highlighted in the
miscellaneous application can only be adjudicated in
a proper proceedings. Further it is relevant to
mention that Committee was constituted as per the
direction of this Court and the Committee after
examining the records available gave the finding on
the illegibility of the candidates. Further it is also
relevant to mention that earlier also this Court gave
direction to the petitioner to submit their PBAS form
for the renewal of their services. The petitioner Mr.
Himanshu Nautiyal concealed the said fact and
obtained the interim order of this Court.
xvii) That Court has failed to consider that the petitioner
no. 2 was engaged by the respondent in the year 2012
and not in 2011."
4) Objections were invited on the said review
applications. The respondent (petitioner no. 2 in the writ
petitions) has filed objections to the same. Composite
objections have, therefore, been filed on behalf of the
opposite parties supported by an affidavit of Dr. Arvind
Kumar Singh on behalf of others also. It is stated in the
composite objections as under:
"i) the petitioners filed contempt application no. 45
of 2016 on 02.03.2016 and on 03.03.2016 notices

9
were issued to the opposite parties. It appears
that after having knowledge received of the
notices the respondents have filed the present
review application.
ii) the respondents deliberately suppressed the
pendency of the contempt proceedings. Since,
the judgment was passed on 01.12.2015, in the
presence of the counsel for the respondents then
what was the occasion to wait for such a long
time even to apply for the certified copy. The
only ground highlighted by them is that they
have changed the counsel. This cannot be said to
a ground for delay in filing the review
applications in time. Thus, on this count the
review applications are liable to be rejected
because after filing of the contempt unless or
until the order complied, they have no right to be
heard. The other reason being that the
respondents want to deprive the petitioners from
the fruits of litigation as the same accrued in their
favour. Apart from this, the present review
applications are filed after the limitation of
review as well as Special Leave Petition(s) and
on this ground also the same are liable to be
rejected.
iii) similarly, by way of review applications the
respondents want the matter to be heard as an
appeal, which is not permissible. Moreover, the
present review applicants have no right to file the
review application because the State Government
has not filed any review or SLP against the
judgment. The principal challenge in the writ

10
petition is against the Government Order by
which the status of the petitioners has been
changed to contractual. The Court has quashed
the G.O., which was the basis of the subsequent
orders of the respondent / review applicant to
alter the status of the petitioners. In their counter
affidavit, the respondents have also taken the
same ground and mentioned that on the basis of
the G.O. the status of the applicant has changed.
Now, when the Court has quashed the G.O., then
the respondents cannot say contrary to this and
on this ground also the review applications are
liable to be rejected.
iv) the contents of paras no. 2 to 7 alongwith
grounds of review from paras no. 1 to 28 taken in
review application no. 182 of 2016 filed in
WPSB no. 294 of 2016 are frivolous and not
tenable in the eyes of law as in the judgment
itself the Court has categorically decided this
question after hearing both the parties. The
review applicants want to argue the review
applications as an appeal, which is not
permissible in law. The ground taken by the
respondents as a ground of review regarding
recommendations of the Committee, which was
not taken into account by the Court, is not
tenable in law because the Court itself appointed
a Committee and examined the report and
considered the objections against the Committee
and thereafter passed the judgment. Thus, it
cannot be treated to be a ground for review.

11
v) similarly, the review application no. 201 of 016
filed by respondent no. 3 is also not tenable for
the same reasons which are highlighted in para
no. 10 of these objections. Moreover, respondent
no. 3 is not entitled to say anything in respect of
the Committee because in the report of the
Committee he himself was a member and also
recommended his case for regularization. The
Court at the time of hearing has taken a note of
the same and thereafter passed the judgment by a
reasoned and speaking order.
vi) also, paras no. 2 to 5 of the affidavit filed in
support of review application as well as grounds
of review application no. 201 of 2016, as
mentioned in paras no. 1 to 15 are not tenable in
view of the reasons highlighted at para no. 10 of
this objection. The review application is only an
attempt to linger on the matter. The grounds no.
15 regarding the year of appointment of the
petitioner no. 2 cannot be ground of review and
only a correction is required. Thus all the review
applications are liable to be dismissed with
costs."
5) First and foremost, it may be noted here that
the State Government has not filed any review
application. The Court has been informed that the
State Government has not even filed any Special Leave
Petition against the judgment. It is only the review
applicants, who have filed these review applications.
The reason seems to be obvious. There is also delay in
filing these review applications, although the reasons

12
are condonable. The Senior Counsel, who has argued
the review applications, did not argue the writ petitions,
probably because he was requested later.
6) The review applications have been filed, as if
they are filing appeals. There is no error apparent on
the face of record, which may be the only main ground
available for review. The review applications have not
taken any ground which is legally available in review.
The same is not tenable. By means of these review
applications, the review applicants seek to re-argue the
writ petitions, which is not permissible in law. Review
applications are, therefore, liable to be dismissed on this
ground alone. The very object of filing these review
applications, seems to be, to deny the fruit of litigation
to the petitioners. There does not appear to be any
plausible reason for filing the same, except to deny
legitimate rights to the petitioners.
7) Learned Senior Counsel for the review
applicants submitted that the Court had directed to
constitute a committee to evaluate the educational
qualifications of petitioners and it was observed that if the
petitioners do not fulfill the required educational
qualification, then it would be in the fitness of things to
consider their services as purely temporary in nature. It is
also the submission of learned Senior Counsel for the
review applicants that the committee found that some of the
petitioners were not eligible and not fit for the posts which
they were occupying.

13
8) The review applicants failed to notice that
this Court never approved the recommendations of the
committee. Law is clear that interim observations or
interim orders simply merge in the final order.
Moreover, as said earlier, the Court never put its seal of
approval on the recommendations of the committee.
9) Further, by means of present review
applications, the review applicants are again agitating the
point that there is no substantive post in the institute,
knowing fully well that this issue has been dealt with, in
detail, by this Court, while deciding the writ petitions. If
there is anything wrong, in the estimation of the review
applicants, then it is open for them to take recourse to
appropriate remedy before the appropriate forum.
10) The issue of MOU has already been discussed
by the Court in the judgment under review. No useful
purpose would be served by challenging the same again
and again before this Court. It will also be a futile exercise
for this Court to justify it's order time and again. Then,
where is the application of law laid down by Hon'ble
Supreme Court in State of Karnataka vs Uma Devi, (2006)
4 SCC 1, to the facts of this case? A ground has been taken
in the review applications that the regularization of the
faculty members is contrary to such a decision, which
appears to be nothing but non-application of mind by the
review applicants to the facts of this case vis-à-vis law laid
down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Uma Devi's case (supra).

14
11) Still further, this Court has adjudicated upon
the issues, which were pleaded by the parties. The Court
has not decided the writ petitions taking cognizance of such
facts, which were not part of such pleadings.
12) No new issue has been pressed, nor arises.
13) To repeat, the review applicants have again
agitated those arguments, which have already been dealt
with by the Court while rendering the decision in writ
petitions.
14) To recapitulate, review is available only on a
limited ground that if there is some mistake or error
apparent on the face of record, the same may be brought to
the notice of the Court. There is no mistake or error
apparent on the face of record which requires review of the
judgment and order dated 01.12.2015.
15) All the review applications are thoroughly
misconceived and are hereby dismissed.
16) With great difficulty, this Court is restraining
itself from imposing heavy cost upon the review applicants.

(U.C. Dhyani, J.) (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dt. July 20, 2016.
Negi
